line: Strength that comes from staying in motion: the fire is back in balance and holds by constant change, as a cyclist stays upright only by going fast enough. It is the strength of a defender who keeps moving, not of a wall. Drawn, the card asks you to stay alert and adaptable, and promises that you can hold your ground if you keep moving with events. The Moon in Sagittarius, weakest planet in the most elusive sign, works here in Yesod, the Foundation.

quotes.quote: This card is also governed by the Moon in Sagittarius; so here is a double influence of the Moon on the Tree of Life. Hence the aphorism “Change is Stability”.
Here the Moon, the weakest of the planets, is in Sagittarius, the most elusive of the Signs; yet it dares call itself Strength. Defence, to be effective, must be mobile.

The Wands have now become arrows. There are eight of them in the background, and in front of them one master arrow. This has the Moon for its point, and the Sun for the driving Force above it; for the path of Sagittarius on the Tree of Life joins the Sun and Moon. The flames in the card are tenfold, implying that the Energy is directed downwards.
These cards are attributed to Yesod. After the double excursion into misfortune, the current returns to the middle pillar. This Sephira is the seat of the great crystallization of Energy.

Of all important doctrines concerning equilibrium, this is the easiest to understand, that change is stability; that stability is guaranteed by change; that if anything should stop changing for the fraction of a split second, it would go to pieces.
